submission.justification: Sensor-T3 has the best resolution (6 um at 150 um) but only 82% efficiency at 2e16 neq/cm^2, so it fails the hard 97% requirement. Of the two remaining options, T1 resolves better than T2 (about 9 um against about 14.8 um at 100 um). A T1 thickness scan gave a minimum near 150 um: 10.18 um at 50, 9.17 at 100, 9.18 at 130, 8.77 at 150, 8.91 at 170, 9.37 at 200, 10.10 at 250 and 11.75 at 300. So I recommend T1 at 150 um. The simulations are unirradiated, so the resolution after irradiation is unverified. The T1 thickness scan is also unirradiated, and the 98.5% efficiency was measured on one sample, whose thickness the document doesn't state. T2 was simulated only at 100 um.

requirements.evidence: T1 at 150 um gives 8.77 um, the best among the technologies that pass the efficiency requirement. T2 gives about 14.8 um at 100 um (14.0 um at 150 um in the 2025 summary). T3 is better but excluded.
The 2026 test beam measured 98.5% for T1. T3 measured 82% and fails. The document doesn't state the thickness of the tested T1 sensors, so the efficiency at 150 um is an assumption.

requirements.requirement: Technology is one of the three candidates
